items.title: DECODE: Decomposable Environments for COntrolled Sequential-Decision Evaluation
items.summary_1line: When a sequential decision system falls short of an optimum, its score does not reveal which modifications would improve its decisions. DECODE is a benchmark for testing such modifications through controlled experimen...
items.editor_note: Extends the approach to sequential decisions, testing which system change helps.

editorial.tldr: This is a research trend, not one developing event: three unrelated groups published benchmarks that change one variable at a time so a failure can be traced to a cause. On Nov 6, KLEAR did this for Korean LLM knowledge questions and AllenAI's ToyBlocks did it for robot learning in a simulated block world.
editorial.whats_new: DECODE (Nov 13) brings controlled evaluation to sequential decision-making, using decomposable environments to test which change to a system actually improves its decisions.
editorial.why_it_matters: A single aggregate score cannot tell you whether an agent failed on missing knowledge, poor planning, or the environment, and these benchmarks are designed to separate those causes.
editorial.take_for_builders: When an agent eval regresses, add ablation cases that change one factor at a time (knowledge, plan length, environment) before you trust the aggregate score.

beats.headline: Two controlled benchmarks land the same day: Korean LLM knowledge and robot learning
beats.summary: KLEAR separates missing knowledge from other error sources. ToyBlocks gives robot policies a controlled world to train and test in.

beats.headline: DECODE applies the same idea to sequential decision systems
beats.summary: Decomposable environments let researchers test whether a specific change to a system improves its decisions.

open_questions: Does a controlled benchmark for LLM agents with tool use appear, separating tool, planning, and knowledge failures?
Do DECODE or KLEAR release code and data that can be run against production models?
Do diagnoses from these controlled setups match what aggregate leaderboards show for the same models?
